name: meshweaver-mobile
description: MeshWeaver on React Native / Expo — the native leaf pack over @meshweaver/react/core. The MAUI peer.

scripts.web:export: expo export --platform web && node scripts/pwa-inject.mjs dist/index.html

_overrides_note: postcss: expo 52 → @expo/metro-config pins 8.4.49, below the 8.5.x patch line. This is the one
advisory in the Expo tree that is BOTH reachable from what we build (the web export bundles CSS
through metro-config) and safe to force — same major, no API change.
The rest of the Expo-toolchain advisories (tar, @xmldom/xmldom, uuid, brace-expansion) are NOT
overridden on purpose: each patched version is a breaking major for its CJS consumer inside
@expo/cli / native prebuild (brace-expansion@5 is ESM-only and minimatch requires() it; uuid@11
likewise breaks xcode's require; tar 6→7 and xmldom 0.7→0.9 are breaking API changes). They are
reachable only from `expo prebuild` / `expo run:*`, not from the web export or the test run.
Forcing them would break the build to quiet a scanner — the real fix is the Expo SDK upgrade
(expo@57 + react-native@0.86), which is its own migration.
_npm_major_holdback_note: This package is deliberately held at the pre-688ce589b versions (expo 52, react 18.3.1,
typescript 5.6). The npm-major sweep bumped expo 52->57 and react 18->19 HERE but PINNED
react-native at 0.76.5, and bumped typescript to 7. Both halves break, for different reasons,
and BOTH were observed on CI rather than reasoned about:
1. react 19 cannot install. react-native@0.76.5 hard-peers react ^18.2.0, so npm ci fails
ERESOLVE and BOTH RN jobs die before running a single check. Probed directly: pinning
@types/react back to 18 does NOT help — npm still reports
Found: react@19.2.8 / peer react@^18.2.0 from react-native@0.76.5
so the blocker is the HARD react peer, not the peerOptional @types/react one that the CI
log surfaces first. --legacy-peer-deps / overrides would install a combination upstream
does not support, and RN web is a Playwright job that actually renders.
2. typescript 7 breaks the web export. @expo/cli (SDK 52) reads tsconfig through the CLASSIC
TypeScript compiler API, which TS 7 deleted along with transpileModule (its '.' export is
now just lib/version.cjs). expo export dies with
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getCurrentDirectory')
at evaluateTsConfig (@expo/cli/src/utils/tsconfig/evaluateTsConfig.ts)
So typescript stays 5.x here until the Expo SDK upgrade. This is the same TS 7 removal
that forced clients/typescript off transpileModule onto amaro.
Moving forward is issue #1584: react-native 0.82 peers are exactly react ^19.1.1 — the Expo
SDK 52->57 upgrade, which also has to port expo-av. Do that deliberately, not by sweep.
